evidence.note: MSS has no website or published email; established by the Security Service Act 1996, operates under ministerial/PM oversight; assumed to use the shared gov.mt mail domain like all Maltese government bodies

entities.notes: Domestic intelligence agency with essentially no public footprint: its only public output is an annual report tabled in Parliament; complaints go through an independent Commissioner. Website given is the parent ministry's.

entities.notes: Ministry name changes frequently: homepage (2026) titles it Ministry for Home Affairs, Security and Employment, while some mid-2026 circulars use 'Ministry for Home Affairs and Security'. It is also the de facto defence ministry: the Armed Forces of Malta fall under its portfolio (Malta has no separate Ministry of Defence). Secondary site sigurta.gov.mt.

gaps: gendarmerie: Malta has no gendarmerie-type force; the Malta Police Force is the single national police body.

border_guard: no standalone border guard agency; the Armed Forces of Malta perform maritime border surveillance (classified under border_guard here), with immigration/border checks handled by the Malta Police Force.
defence_ministry: Malta has no separate Ministry of Defence; the Armed Forces of Malta fall under the Ministry for Home Affairs, Security and Employment.
intelligence: the Malta Security Service has no website and no published email address; its gov.mt mail domain is assumed (confidence low).
All Maltese government entities use the single shared mail domain gov.mt; no entity-specific mail domains exist, which limits per-entity email-sovereignty differentiation.
